answer: Each identity must raise one stone cairn on a distinct ridge, marked with opal pigment that only that ridge's quarry can grind: the k-th cairn needs k cubed stones, so fake k pays k^3. Ten fakes pay 3,025 stones; a hundred pay 25,502,500, growing cubically. Two cairns sharing one ridge collapse each other and both are struck, so the cost cannot be pooled across clones.
